A deep mossy canyon carved by centuries of slow water, its sheer green walls dropping forty feet to a glowing amber stream below, ferns cascading from every ledge in soft curtains.
A tumbling four-tier waterfall spilling down a black basalt face, each tier pooling before overflowing the next, spray hanging in the air like fine gauze, the whole cliff-face furred in vivid moss.
A winding glowing stream threading through pale rounded stones, its pools lit aquamarine from below, the banks thick with soft fern and clover, small cascades murmuring between each quiet basin.

A cluster of colossal mossy boulders half the size of cottages, tumbled together in ancient disorder, deep shadow-gaps between them draped in hanging fern, a thin trickle of water weeping down the largest face.

A sheer mossy cliff-face rising sixty feet from the forest floor, its surface a living tapestry of green and gold, water seeping in silver threads down the stone, swallows nesting in the high crevices.
A grove of colossal ancient trees with bark like folded grey cliffs, their roots arching clear of the ground in enormous buttresses, the canopy so vast it holds its own soft inland weather of mist.

A rocky river-island splitting a wide amber current into two gentle arms, the island itself crowded with willow and birch, its upstream tip a bare wedge of pale stone worn smooth by centuries of water.
A misty ravine barely three paces wide but deep enough to lose the sky, its hanging gardens of fern and moss dripping from both walls, a faint cold air rising from the darkness far below.

A sea-cliff standing above turquoise shallows, its face striped pale gold and iron-red, the base undercut into dark arching hollows where the sea breathes slowly in and out, salt-spray dusting the clifftop meadow.

A tumbled rock-scree slope descending from a high grey ridge, its boulders furred in pale lichen and cushion-moss, small wildflowers finding root in every crack, the whole slope glowing faint silver in afternoon light.
A cave-mouth grotto set into a hillside, its entrance draped in hanging moss and maidenhair fern, a cold clear spring pooling just inside before spilling out across smooth stone into the open air.

A chain of rocky islets stepping across a wide tidal channel, each one barely large enough for a single ancient pine, the pale stone scoured clean at its base, the tops crowded with roots and green shadow.

Terraced hot-spring pools descending a mineral hillside in pale stone steps, each pool a different shade from cream to deep jade, steam rising in slow columns, the surrounding rock crusted in orange and ivory mineral bloom.

A fern-choked rocky creek-bed threading through a low ravine, its stones copper-red and grey beneath the clear shallow water, mossy ledges overhung with bracken, the whole channel cool and green as a held breath.

A forested rocky outcrop rising sharply from flat meadow, its flanks thick with oak and rowan rooted in every crack, the bare summit a single weathered shelf of pale stone looking out across a wide green valley.

A deep glowing sinkhole garden, its circular walls dropping thirty feet in rings of layered stone laced with fern and wildflower, a hidden pool at the bottom catching the single column of sky-light far above.

A broad granite dome rising smooth from the forest, its bare crown polished by old glaciers to a pale gleam, shallow pools collected in its hollows reflecting open sky, the surrounding trees pressing close at its base.

A narrow slot canyon barely wide enough for a person, its pale sandstone walls curving in smooth organic folds, a thread of turquoise water on the sand floor, light entering only as a bright ribbon high above.
A collapsed sea-arch leaving a single dramatic standing pillar of dark rock in the shallows, its top colonized by turf and sea-pink, waves folding white around its base in soft repeating sighs.

A high mountain tarn set in a bowl of bare grey rock, its water ink-dark and utterly still, reflecting the surrounding ridgeline in perfect silence, a fringe of low sedge and heather at its marshy edge.

A basalt organ-pipe cliff rising from the forest like a great broken wall, its hexagonal columns fitted together in vast imperfect geometry, mosses and small ferns softening every horizontal joint with green.

A wide shallow river braided across a pale gravel bed, its many channels glinting between low islands of alder and willow, the water quick and clear over smooth stones, the whole broad valley floor alive with soft sound.

A limestone pavement terrace above a wooded valley, its cracked grey surface fissured into deep grikes choked with hart's-tongue fern and wild garlic, the whole plateau pale and luminous under an open sky.

A hanging valley high above the main glen, its floor flat and green with a slow meander, the far end dropping suddenly over a long thin waterfall that dissolves to mist long before it reaches the valley below.

A cathedral grove of ancient yew trees, their trunks twisted to dark columns, the canopy closing out the sky entirely, the floor bare red earth in the deep shade, a profound interior silence held within the ring of living wood.
